papers.title: Historical higher-order collaboration topology and inventor-level patent outcomes
papers.abstract: Collaborators appearing together on an inventor’s current patents may have very different histories of joint patenting. Using 774,371 inventor–year observations from 82,926 inventors in USPTO utility patent data, we construct event-based simplicial complexes of prior patenting among each inventor’s current collaborators. The zeroth Betti number ( $\beta _{0}$ β 0 ) counts connected components that are also observable in pairwise graphs, whereas the first Betti number ( $\beta _{1}$ β 1 ) identifies unfilled cycles that depend on joint-event information. We examine these complementary descriptors in relation to inventor-level patent outcomes, with Inventors’ Disruptive Citations (IDC) as the principal citation outcome. After adjustment for collaborator-set size and other covariates, $\beta _{0}$ β 0 exhibits a fitted inverted-U-shaped association with IDC: expected IDC increases over most observed component counts but at a diminishing rate, while the fitted decline lies in a sparsely populated upper tail. The presence of unfilled cycles is associated with modestly higher cumulative IDC ( $\mathrm{IRR} = 1.077$ IRR = 1.077 ), although this positive association does not persist after accounting for contemporaneous patenting volume. Similar fitted $\beta _{0}$ β 0 patterns appear for consolidating citations, the inventor–year Total CD index, productivity and claim count. $\beta _{1}$ β 1 is positively associated with the latter three outcomes, but its association with consolidating citations is uncertain. The $\beta _{0}$ β 0 –IDC association varies across 13 application periods and Main CPC sections A–H. The findings describe outcome-dependent associations of historical collaboration connectivity and event-dependent topology, with limited incremental fit for cumulative IDC.

papers.title: From first principles to multi-scale decomposition: mutual information as a segregation index
papers.abstract: Segregation operates across demographic and spatial scales and requires careful and principled measurement. In this work, we derive mutual information from well-known general approaches to constructing segregation indices and interpret the mathematical properties that are unique to it. The properties relate mainly to its behaviour when demographic identities and spatial units are coarse-grained. Mutual information decomposes into the contributions of regions and supergroups, which reveals insights that would be inaccessible otherwise. We demonstrate this with an exploratory case study of residential ethnic segregation in England and Wales. Overall, we help researchers identify when mutual information is the only suitable segregation index and provide open source software to support multi-scale analysis.

papers.title: Large language models' complicit responses to illicit instructions across socio-legal contexts
papers.abstract: Large language models may facilitate unlawful activities, yet this risk remains underexplored in studies assessing illicit-content recognition or narrow categories of illicit scenarios. We define complicit facilitation as model guidance that assists users with illicit instructions. To assess it, we develop a legally-informed, automated pipeline grounded in real-world cases and legal frameworks, and introduce EVIL, a benchmark covering 269 illicit scenarios and 50 illicit intents across Chinese and United States legal contexts. Evaluations indicate that complicit facilitation is widespread across models, with legal warnings and lawful alternatives often omitted. Risks vary across socio-legal contexts and are elevated for crimes against societal interests, non-violent offenses, and intents involving subjective motives or deceptive justifications. Models provide more complicit assistance when instructions describe users as older adults, racial minorities, non-religious individuals, or workers in lower-prestige occupations. Existing open-source safety benchmarks and alignment datasets offer limited coverage and mitigation of these risks.
papers.tldr_zh: 构建跨中美法律语境的269个非法场景基准EVIL，评测发现大模型普遍对非法指令提供协助性回应。
papers.reason: 系统评测大模型在非法指令下的行为风险，对LLM社会影响与平台治理研究有实证价值。

papers.title: Automated data to model transformation for constraint programming with AI
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence for combinatorial optimization depends on high-quality, structured training data, yet transforming ambiguous natural-language descriptions into precise, executable formal models remains a major bottleneck, traditionally requiring extensive manual effort and domain expertise. We develop CPAM-LLM, an automated constraint-programming modeling framework based on large language models that converts unstructured problem specifications into validated and executable formal models. The framework integrates retrieval-augmented generation grounded in formal concept analysis for structural validation, chaos-mapping-based data augmentation to enhance cross-domain generalization, and dynamic constraint adaptation to accommodate evolving problem settings. We demonstrate its effectiveness across five scenarios, including DNA sequence design, reconfigurable energy storage systems, and unmanned vehicle logistics. The results show that the framework can automate the data-to-model pipeline while adapting reliably to changing requirements, providing a practical approach to automated data formalization and indicating the importance of accessible, high-quality structured data for reliable downstream artificial intelligence applications.
